title: Dedicated fleet cost-curve modeling and automated rightsizing playbook
creator: Marisol Reyes
description:
Background: Customers with Dedicated pools often over-provision to avoid throughput shortfalls during peaks, resulting in predictable but avoidable reserved-GPU cost. Existing reports show large tail reservations and underutilized windows. This initiative will build a reproducible cost-curve model, short-term utilization forecasts, and an automated rightsizing recommender that suggests reserve adjustments and autoscale policy templates.

Goals:
- Produce per-pool cost vs. latency risk curves (percentile-based) and an actionable recommendation (increase/decrease commit) with confidence band.
- Surface recommendations in Console and provide CSV/JSON export for finance & procurement.
- Provide autoscaling policy templates that align with the recommended commit (e.g., baseline commit + burst policies + cooldowns).
- Reduce wasted reserved GPU hours across pilot customers by >=20% within first 60 days while keeping P99 latency regressions <= 5%.

Approach:
1) Data: ingest 90d of per-pool time-series (requests, qps, token throughput, active slots, evictions, latency percentiles) from warehouse.
2) Modeling: build cost-curve generator that computes cost at different percentiles (median, p90, p95, p99) using simulated reserve levels and autoscaler behavior. Use bootstrapped confidence intervals to avoid one-off spikes driving recommendations.
3) Recommender: Rule-based + lightweight ML classifier to flag low-confidence cases (rare traffic patterns, heavy tail) and fall back to conservative suggestions.
4) UX: Console surface with 'Suggested Commit' card, an interactive slider showing cost vs risk, and export button.
5) Ops: runbook for SRE and Sales Eng with rollback steps and canary deployment guidance.

Deliverables:
- API endpoint (internal) that returns cost-curve and recommended commit for a given pool id.
- Daily batch job that computes recommendations and stores history for auditing.
- Console card prototype + export.
- Internal playbook document and customer-ready one-pager.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in average reserved-GPU idle hours for pilot pools.
- >75% of recommendations accepted by internal SEs during pilot.
- No more than 5% increase in p99 latency for pools where commit was reduced.

Constraints/Assumptions:
- We assume accurate mapping from requests -> GPU-hour consumption. Edge cases (bursting external traffic) will be classified as low-confidence.
- Legal/procurement constraints around changing commits require exportable justification artifacts for customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API returns cost-curve and a single recommended commit with confidence metadata for any active dedicated pool id.
2) Console shows recommendation card and allows CSV export of the underlying time-series and reasoning.
3) Batch history retained at least 90 days and queryable via internal API for audits.
4) Pilot run across 6 pools demonstrates >=20% reduction in wasted reserved hours without violating p99 latency SLO (>95% of checks pass).
5) Playbook and runbook approved by SRE and Sales Eng and linked in Console help pane.
